attacks.name: AI Fabricated Identity
attacks.what_attacker_needs: A generative model, a handful of real customer profiles to imitate, and a way to submit new accounts (open API or web form).
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Each individual transaction looks statistically normal because the AI copies real spending shape. There is no prior history to compare against, so rules based on velocity don't fire on transaction #1.
attacks.damage: New account fraud, promo abuse, mule accounts used to launder stolen funds.
attacks.simulated_by: agent1_fake_identity, real OpenAI GPT-4o-mini calls generating each identity

attacks.name: Spending Pattern Replication (Card Testing & Draining)
attacks.what_attacker_needs: A stolen card number or token, and a generator that mimics the cardholder's usual amount/merchant/timing shape while executing at machine speed.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Amounts and merchants resemble genuine history; the anomaly is velocity and cumulative volume, which only shows up in aggregate, not per transaction.
attacks.damage: Direct monetary loss, chargebacks, card network penalties.

attacks.name: Payment Form / API Fuzzing
attacks.stage: Client side input into backend processing
attacks.what_attacker_needs: Knowledge of the form/API schema and an automated fuzzer that throws malformed, oversized, or injection style payloads at each field.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Individually loud and easy to flag, but attackers use it as reconnaissance: the one field that doesn't reject cleanly becomes the entry point for a quieter attack later.
attacks.damage: Backend crashes, injection vulnerabilities, data exposure, or a discovered bypass used in a later attack.
attacks.simulated_by: agent6_injection_generator, known public payloads, no LLM needed

attacks.name: AI Voice/Chat Social Engineering
attacks.what_attacker_needs: A voice cloning or conversational model, some public/leaked personal data about the victim, and a target support channel.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Convincingly mimics a real customer's voice or writing style well enough to pass authentication questions based on personal knowledge.
attacks.damage: Account takeover, unauthorized card issuance, disabled fraud alerts.
attacks.simulated_by: agent2_social_engineer, real OpenAI calls generating text call transcripts only. No voice cloning, no audio, no real support line contacted

attacks.name: Authorization Limit Probing
attacks.what_attacker_needs: A stolen card and a script that submits many small transactions across merchants to map out fraud detection thresholds before making one large charge.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Each probe is small enough to sit under thresholds set per transaction; the pattern only becomes visible when probes are correlated across merchants.
attacks.damage: Reveals the exact threshold defenders use, which is then exploited in a larger, precisely sized fraudulent charge.
attacks.simulated_by: agent3_limit_prober, real: submits amounts $10 to $10,000 through our own trained detector and reads back its real decision boundary. See the Red Team tab

attacks.name: AI Generated KYC Document Forgery
attacks.what_attacker_needs: An image generation model capable of producing plausible ID documents or selfies that pass automated liveness/document checks.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Generated documents can be tuned specifically to defeat the exact verification model in use if the attacker has query access to it.
attacks.damage: Bypasses KYC entirely, enabling fully synthetic identities to open accounts that pass verification.
attacks.simulated_by: agent4_kyc_forger, real OpenAI calls generating identity metadata bundles only, no document images, then scored by our own detector

attacks.name: Feedback Loop Poisoning of the Fraud Model
attacks.what_attacker_needs: Repeated small transactions plus false dispute/chargeback signals designed to teach the detector's retraining pipeline to treat fraud patterns as normal.
attacks.why_hard_to_catch: Attacks the training data, not the transaction. By the time it's visible, the model itself has drifted toward tolerating the fraud pattern.
attacks.damage: Long term degradation of detection accuracy; hardest to detect because the model's own confidence goes up, not down.
attacks.simulated_by: not simulated in this lab. Agent 7 (Feedback Loop Exploit) is related but distinct: it generates real-time evasion variants against the trained model, it does not poison a retraining pipeline. Flagged as a known gap; see docs/how_it_works.txt
